quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #9
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: Traffic signals sometimes show arrows to control turns from specific lanes. What does a green arrow mean?

options.text: It is used only on one-way streets.
It means the same as a green light, but you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
You may proceed only if the green arrow appears with a circular green light.
It points the way to an airport.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same as a green light, but you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means the same as a circular green light. However, traffic in that lane must turn in the direction the arrow shows.

questions.question: When must you yield for emergency vehicles?

options.text: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
questions.explanation: You must let emergency vehicles pass whenever you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road is closed to traffic.

questions.explanation: Orange construction signs warn drivers about work areas ahead. They tell you to slow down and drive carefully in the construction zone.

questions.question: If you are in an accident and someone is injured, what should you do?

options.text: Move the injured person away from the scene right away.
Always leave the injured person where they are.
Do not move the injured person unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
Stay away from the injured person.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not move the injured person unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
questions.explanation: Do not move an injured person unless you must. Moving them the wrong way can make small injuries worse. Keep them warm and stop any bleeding with direct pressure until help arrives.

questions.question: Every vehicle in Minnesota must have liability insurance.
questions.explanation: You must carry proof of insurance in your vehicle at all times. If you cannot show it to a police officer, your driver license and vehicle registration may be suspended.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your view.

questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when behind a large vehicle that blocks your view, in bad weather or heavy traffic, when exiting an expressway, when behind a motorcycle or bicycle, or when someone is tailgating you.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed at this location.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Driving slower reduces the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: What color lines divide traffic moving in opposite directions?
questions.explanation: Yellow lines divide traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: If you stop at a railroad crossing with multiple tracks, what should you do?

options.text: Wait until you can see all tracks clearly before crossing.
Stop on the first track and watch for another train.
Go through as soon as the train passes.
Go through when one track is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all tracks clearly before crossing.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with multiple tracks, do not move until you have a clear view of all tracks. Another train may be coming even after the first train passes. Check all directions before crossing.

questions.question: Can drivers pass on a two-lane road with a single solid yellow line on their side?
questions.explanation: You can only pass when the yellow line nearest to your lane is broken. A solid yellow line on your side means you cannot pass.

questions.question: At night, when another vehicle is coming toward you, what should you do with your headlights?

options.text: Turn them off and use parking lights.
Use either high or low beam.

questions.explanation: Switch to low beam headlights when approaching or following another vehicle at night. High beams can blind other drivers and are unsafe.

questions.question: When must you stop for a school bus?

options.text: When it is parked on the shoulder with no one in it.
Whenever it approaches you, even without flashing lights.
When you are on a two-lane highway and its red lights are flashing.
Whenever the driver waves at you.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are on a two-lane highway and its red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: Stop when a school bus displays flashing red lights on a two-lane road. Traffic in both directions must stop. Stay stopped while the red lights flash and the stop arm is extended.

questions.question: Which traffic light means you should slow down and be careful at an intersection?
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, look both ways, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Parking spaces for people with disabled parking permits.
Traffic in this lane must turn in the direction shown.
Lanes reserved for buses and carpools.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parking spaces for people with disabled parking permits.
questions.explanation: This sign marks parking spaces reserved for people with disabled parking permits only.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You are entering a one-way street the wrong way.
Do not drive in this lane.
Left-turning traffic must let oncoming traffic go first on a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left-turning traffic must let oncoming traffic go first on a green light.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers turning left on green that they do not have the right-of-way. Wait for oncoming traffic to pass before turning.

questions.question: What does a red circle with a line through it on a sign mean?

options.text: The action shown is not allowed.
Some drivers must yield to others.
Drive slower than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: The action shown is not allowed.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a slash means the action is forbidden. These regulatory signs are white with red and black markings.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic signal is the same as:
questions.explanation: A flashing red signal requires you to stop and let other traffic pass before going.

questions.question: When can you drink alcohol in a vehicle on a public highway?

options.text: As long as you are not driving.
If you are in the back seat.
If you are in the back of a pickup truck.

questions.explanation: It is illegal to drink or have an open alcoholic beverage in any vehicle on a public road. This applies to all passengers and drivers.

questions.question: What does a red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: Stop and then go when the way is clear.
Stop and wait for a green light or green arrow.
You can turn in the direction the arrow points.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait for a green light or green arrow.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means stop completely. Stay stopped until a green light or green arrow appears, unless a sign says otherwise.

questions.question: Drivers do not have to yield to pedestrians who are crossing against the traffic light.
questions.explanation: You must always yield to pedestrians. Pedestrians may sometimes cross against the light by mistake. Stay alert and yield to them anyway.

questions.question: When dealing with pedestrians, a driver must:

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian sees you.
Always yield, even if the pedestrian is wrong.
Yield only when the pedestrian has the right-of-way.
Slow down and honk near a crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always yield, even if the pedestrian is wrong.
questions.explanation: You must do everything possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian or another vehicle, no matter what. It is your job as a driver to watch for pedestrians and yield to them. This is true even if they are crossing illegally.

questions.question: A driver entering a highway from an entrance or acceleration ramp:

options.text: Should yield to drivers already on the highway.
May force their way into traffic.
Can assume other drivers will move for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should yield to drivers already on the highway.
questions.explanation: When entering a highway from an entrance or acceleration ramp, yield to traffic already on the highway. Merge safely when there is a gap in traffic.

questions.question: Night driving requires extra caution because:

options.text: There is more traffic at night.
Accidents happen more often at night.

questions.explanation: It is dark at night, so you cannot see as far or as clearly. You must use your headlights from 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise, or whenever objects cannot be seen 500 feet ahead.

questions.question: Two solid yellow lines on the road mean:

options.text: Drivers from both directions can pass.
Passing is allowed at the top of a hill.
Passing is allowed during the day only.

questions.explanation: Yellow lines mean traffic on the other side is going the opposite direction. Never cross two solid yellow lines to pass from either direction.

questions.question: A solid yellow line on your side of the center means:
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line next to your lane means you cannot pass other vehicles from your direction.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection, a driver must yield to a bicyclist coming from the opposite direction.
questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to oncoming bicycles just as you would yield to oncoming cars. Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn. Turn only when the intersection is clear.

questions.question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches you on a one-way street, you must:

options.text: Move to the nearest side and stop.
Speed up and take the next exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the nearest side and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with lights or siren approaches on a one-way street, move to the nearest side of the road and stop.

questions.question: When passing other vehicles, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
Honk your horn at least three times.
Return to your lane within 10 feet of the other vehicle.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check your mirrors and blind spots. Use your turn signal before changing lanes. Return to your lane only when you can see the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: In icy or snowy conditions, which technique helps drivers avoid crashes?

options.text: Add extra weight to improve traction.
Leave the highway as soon as possible.
Reduce speed and increase following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce speed and increase following distance.
questions.explanation: Slow down on snowy or icy roads. Reducing speed and increasing your following distance are the best ways to avoid crashes in bad weather.

questions.question: If you miss your turn or exit on a freeway, what should you do?

options.text: Make a quick turn from your current lane.
Keep driving until you reach the next turn, exit, or safe place to turn around.
Signal other drivers to stop so you can turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep driving until you reach the next turn, exit, or safe place to turn around.
questions.explanation: Do not back up if you miss your turn or exit. Instead, drive to the next turn or exit where you can safely turn around. Backing up on a freeway shoulder is illegal.

questions.question: What is the "No zone"?

options.text: The blind spots around a truck or bus.
A road with restrictions on stereo volume.

questions.correctAnswerText: The blind spots around a truck or bus.
questions.explanation: Trucks and buses have blind spots on both sides, in the rear, and in the front. Your car cannot be seen in these areas. These blind spots are called the "No zone."

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot enter the road or driveway from your current direction. If you see this sign, turn around and choose a different route.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lines mean you may pass another vehicle from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no vehicle can cross the center line to pass, no matter which direction you are traveling.

questions.question: If two drivers arrive at the same time to a four-way stop sign intersection, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: One driver may go without stopping.
One driver should honk to give up the right-of-way.

questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, if two drivers arrive at the same time, the driver on your right has the right-of-way. You can go when it is safe.

questions.question: Can drivers park in the access aisles next to handicap parking spaces?
questions.explanation: You cannot park in handicap access aisles. These aisles provide space for wheelchairs and wheelchair lifts.

questions.question: What is distracted driving?

options.text: Just as safe as regular driving.

questions.explanation: Distracted driving is very dangerous. It puts you, your passengers, pedestrians, cyclists, and other drivers at risk. Staying focused on the road helps prevent crashes.

questions.question: The space you need to cross traffic depends on what factors?

options.text: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.
Whether there is a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: The space you need to cross traffic depends on road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on yellow backgrounds. They warn you about upcoming hazards. This sign tells you a traffic light is ahead, so prepare to stop at a red or yellow light.

questions.question: If your car skids on water, should you quickly apply the brakes?
questions.explanation: If your car hydroplanes and skids, do not apply the brakes right away. Instead, try to regain control. If you cannot, release the accelerator and let the skid stop on its own.
